question: What is the primary cellular change that initiates cancer development?

options.A: Rapid cell death caused by bacterial infections
options.B: Normal replacement of aging cells by healthy tissue
options.C: Uncontrolled cell multiplication due to genetic mutations
options.D: Permanent shrinkage of tissues due to poor blood supply

explanation: Cancer starts when genetic changes cause cells to divide uncontrollably and form abnormal masses. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is the initial diagnostic phase particularly stressful for patients?

options.A: Hospital discharge planners force patients to relocate permanently
options.B: Treatment medications cause immediate physical weakness and hair loss
options.C: Diagnostic procedures require prolonged confinement in isolation wards
options.D: Patients face uncertainty and fear regarding potential outcomes

explanation: The suspicion of a life-threatening illness creates significant emotional turmoil and anxiety for the patient and family. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h1)

question: The main goal of cancer screening programs in healthy populations is to...

options.B: lower the financial cost of hospital care

explanation: Screening is designed to catch cancer early when treatment is most effective. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for an endoscopic evaluation of the upper gastrointestinal tract needs nursing preparation that includes...

options.A: administering a high-protein meal before the test
options.B: ensuring the patient walks actively for two hours
options.C: restricting all oral fluids for exactly one week
options.D: verifying informed consent and fasting status

explanation: Endoscopic procedures require an empty stomach to ensure clear visualization and prevent aspiration risks. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h2)

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?
explanation: In TNM staging, M indicates whether the cancer has spread to distant organs in the body. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h3)

question: How does a Grade 4 tumor differ functionally from a Grade 1 tumor?

options.A: Grade 4 growths respond instantly to mild dietary changes
options.B: Grade 4 cells look highly abnormal and multiply rapidly
options.C: Grade 4 tumors never spread beyond the local tissue site
options.D: Grade 4 cells resemble normal healthy tissue very closely

explanation: Higher tumor grades indicate poorly differentiated, aggressive cells that grow and spread quickly. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is a tissue biopsy considered essential in cancer diagnosis?

options.A: It provides definitive microscopic proof of malignancy
options.B: It completely cures the patient without further drugs
options.C: It replaces the need for any blood investigations
options.D: It eliminates all post-operative pain immediately

explanation: Only direct examination of cellular tissue by a pathologist can definitively confirm the presence of cancer cells. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h4)

question: Immediately after obtaining a surgical tissue specimen, the nurse must...

options.A: store it inside a standard household refrigerator overnight
options.B: leave the specimen exposed to air on the procedure tray
options.C: wash the tissue sample thoroughly with sterile tap water
options.D: place it in the proper fixative solution and label it accurately

explanation: Proper fixation prevents tissue degradation and accurate labeling prevents dangerous diagnostic mix-ups. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which nursing action is most critical immediately following a liver biopsy?

options.A: Administering a large oral dose of routine laxatives
options.B: Placing a hot water bottle directly over the puncture site
options.C: Encouraging immediate ambulation around the hospital ward
options.D: Positioning the patient on the right side to apply pressure

explanation: Lying on the right side helps tamponade the liver capsule against the abdominal wall to minimize bleeding risks. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h5)

question: A common post-procedural complication that nurses must monitor for after a core needle biopsy is...
explanation: Because biopsies disrupt tissue and blood vessels, bleeding is a primary risk that requires vigilant monitoring. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h5)

question: How can a nurse best help a patient experiencing severe anxiety while waiting for biopsy results?

options.A: Reassure the patient firmly that the laboratory results will be normal
options.B: Provide a quiet, supportive environment and listen attentively to fears
options.C: Advise the patient to avoid asking questions about the disease
options.D: Keep the patient heavily sedated until the final report arrives

explanation: Active listening and calm reassurance validate patient feelings without making false promises about medical outcomes. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h6)

question: A physical sign that frequently accompanies high levels of diagnostic-related anxiety is...

options.A: persistent insomnia and elevated heart rate
options.B: profound slowing of the resting pulse rate
options.C: sudden increase in normal daily appetite
options.D: extreme muscle relaxation and deep sleep

explanation: Anxiety activates the sympathetic nervous system, leading to physiological symptoms like tachycardia and sleep disturbances. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team approach essential in the management of newly diagnosed cancer?

options.A: It removes the need for nurses to communicate with the patient family
options.B: It allows the hospital administration to reduce total nursing staff numbers
options.C: It ensures that surgical procedures are performed without any assistance
options.D: It combines diverse expert knowledge to create a comprehensive treatment plan

explanation: Cancer care is complex, requiring input from doctors, nurses, and specialists to address all aspects of the disease. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h7)

question: A primary responsibility of the oncology nurse within the multidisciplinary team is to...

options.A: coordinate patient care and bridge communication between specialists
options.B: perform independent pathological analysis of tissue slides
options.C: make the final decision regarding chemotherapy drug dosages
options.D: prescribe specialized radiological scans for staging purposes

explanation: Nurses spend the most time with patients, placing them in the ideal position to coordinate care and relay information. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h7)
